claims.text: Si3N4 or Al2O3 can serve as a high-strength ceramic matrix.
A pure Si3N4 or Al2O3 matrix exhibits insufficient lubrication at elevated temperatures.
The proposed intervention is addition of 5–10 vol% nanostructured hBN to a Si3N4 or Al2O3 matrix.
The proposed composite is sintered at approximately 1600°C.
The intended operating and testing range is 500–1000°C under mechanical loading.
Processing will produce nanostructured hBN particles dispersed within the ceramic matrix.
Dispersed hBN will form a continuous, layered solid-lubricating film at high temperatures.
The hBN-derived film will reduce friction during sliding contact.
The hBN addition and resulting film will not significantly compromise the load-bearing ceramic structure.
The hBN-containing composite will have a lower friction coefficient than the pure ceramic matrix in the 500–1000°C range.
The hBN-containing composite will have better wear resistance than the pure ceramic matrix in the 500–1000°C range.
The hBN-containing composite will maintain mechanical strength across 500–1000°C.
Ceramic composites without hBN typically exhibit degraded lubrication or compromised strength at high temperatures.
The predicted benefits are limited to Si3N4 or Al2O3 matrices operated at 500–1000°C.
Performance outside 500–1000°C or in other ceramic systems may differ from the prediction.
Cyclic thermal and mechanical stress may limit the long-term stability of the hBN-derived lubricating film.
Variations in hBN dispersion uniformity may cause variability in composite performance.
